bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly to Annual: The Basics

If you’re a nurse in New South Wales looking at a job offer or trying to budget, the first step is understanding how your hourly rate translates into annual pay. The standard formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For full-time employees, we assume a 38-hour week, which is the ordinary hours under the Fair Work Act. So annual gross ≈ hourly rate × 38 × 52.

For example, if you earn $40 per hour, your annual gross would be $40 × 38 × 52 = $79,040. This figure does not include superannuation, which is paid on top, or any penalty rates, allowances, or overtime. It’s a base estimate to help you compare offers.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many nurses are paid fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the same $40/hour example, weekly pay is $40 × 38 = $1,520, so fortnightly gross is $3,040. This is before tax and any deductions.

## Minimum Wage, Awards, and Casual Loading

Australia has a National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. However, most nurses are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. The Nurses Award 2020, for example, has specific pay rates based on classification and experience. When using [the timesheet](/), you should enter your base hourly rate as stated in your award or contract. If you are casual, tick the casual loading checkbox to add 25% on top. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

### State Differences: Nurse Salary NSW

When researching “nurse salary NSW”, you’ll often see averages from the Australian Bureau of Statistics. The ABS reports that full-time adult ordinary time earnings in New South Wales were $2,108.80 per week in May 2026. This is an average across all full-time employees in NSW, not a median for nurses. It is higher than the national average of $2,083.70 per week. While this gives a general sense of earnings in the state, your actual pay depends on your award classification, experience, and employer.

For a more tailored estimate, use [reference tables](/data) that list award rates for nurses. Remember that the ABS figure is an average, not a median for your specific job.

## Tax and Medicare

Once you have your annual gross, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates. The tax-free threshold is $18,200. From there:
- 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% on income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% on income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. For a nurse earning $79,040, tax would be approximately $13,717 plus Medicare of $1,581, leaving about $63,742 after tax. This is an estimate only.

## Superannuation

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. For the $79,040 example, your employer would contribute $9,484.80 into your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it’s additional. You can learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Casual vs Permanent

If you are a casual nurse, your hourly rate includes a 25% loading to compensate for lack of paid leave. When converting to annual, use the loaded rate. For example, a casual nurse with a base award rate of $35/hour would enter $35 in [the timesheet](/), tick casual loading, and the calculator will use $43.75 per hour. The annual estimate will be higher, but remember that casual work may not guarantee 38 hours every week.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, Medicare levy surcharge and salary packaging not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more details on [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) and [average pay](/topics/average-pay) guides, visit our site.
